thread:
Alex: Quick sync—I'm putting up a short plan to peel the enrichment hotpath into a read-only sidecar + lightweight ingestion facade. Goal is to shrink the hot path and make stateful ownership explicit. RFC link: https://rfd.internal/enrich-sidecar (WIP).
Maria: Curious on scope. Are we just moving KV access or also the realtime transform logic? :thinking:
Alex: Both initially. KV access + prefix caching stays with the sidecar. Transform logic split into two: deterministic transforms to sidecar, heuristics stay in offline workers.
Ben: How do we handle versioned transforms during rollout? We can't afford mismatched outputs on canary vs prod.
Alex: Plan is: 1) sidecar exposes /transform?version=V endpoint 2) router has model-aware headers 3) canary traffic routed to variant v2 while v1 stays default.
Sasha: Can we avoid per-request version query param? That adds cardinality. Maybe use header: X-Enrich-Version. Router can set it.
Maria: Agree on header. Also need a migration story for cached prefixes—if transform semantics change, cache keys must be invalidated.
Alex: Yep. Add cache version to keys: enrich:v{version}:{prefix_hash}. Simple and explicit.
Ben: What about latency SLOs? Sidecar adds extra network hop for many services. Have numbers?
Alex: Benchmarks from the spike: local same-host sidecar median +3ms, cross-host +9ms under p95 load. We'll aim to collocate for hot tenants, autoscale sidecar pool.
Sasha: Autoscale policy suggestion: scale by p50 reqs/sec and target p95 < 25ms. Also limit batch size to keep tail predictable.
Maria: We should also flag deprecated callers. Some services read/write directly to enrichment DB—those paths need a migration plan before cutover.
Alex: Agreed. Migration checklist draft attached in RFC. Short version: advertise deprecation, two-week read-mirror phase, one-week shadow writes, rollback window.
Ben: Any DB schema changes? If we introduce cache_version field we need migration lockstep.
Alex: No schema changes required if we treat cache key versioning at application layer. But if we optimize by adding a small version col, we'll coordinate with infra for a low-risk deploy.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: spike results uploaded to #eng-runtime: https://ci.internal/build/3321, perf artifacts in s3://redwood-infra/enrich-spike/1746123456
Sasha: One more ops ask: add a circuit-breaker that falls back to the old path when sidecar p95 > 200ms or error rate > 1%. We need graceful fallback for tenant traffic.
Alex: On it. Will add to rollout: canary with fallback and automated rollback trigger.
Maria: Thx. Can we split the work into three milestones? Milestone A: sidecar interface + router header support. B: cache key versioning + migration. C: rollout & ops (autoscale + circuit-breaker).
Ben: Sounds good. I'll volunteer to own Milestone B.
Sasha: I'll help with autoscale/circuit-breaker tests.
Alex: Great. I'll update RFC with milestones and owners, aim to start work next sprint. :thumbsup:
